chapter: Maynard Ferguson and the drinking life
title: Joining Maynard Ferguson's band and the Cleveland high school incident
summary: Called through Linc Milliman, he joins Maynard Ferguson's loose band, with a story about a clinic dispute and smoke bombs, versus the Glenn Miller band's strict rules.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: So, but Linc Milliman had come to my high school because he had gone to Fredonia with Don Menza, who had gotten him on Maynard’s band, and he came here because he was a school friend of the choral director. And I met him. And then I worked with him off and on with Jack Maheu’s Salt City Six. And Randy did — now an English band becoming an American band again — half English, half American. Randy Jones was the drummer. And he was leaving. So the bass player, Rick Petrone, asked Linc if he knew any drummers. He said, “yeah, call Danny D’Imperio.” So now I’m getting on the bandstand with Gap and the phone rings in the bar and they wanted me to come with the band. And I get up on the bandstand with Gap and I said, “Maynard Ferguson needs a drummer.” He said, “tell him to call the union.” In other words, he was PO’d because he didn’t want me to drop out. But I had always wanted to play with Maynard’s band. Even though the band was in transition, it wasn’t the “Rocky” band yet. It was the “Chameleon” band you know. I did that with him. We were still playing quite a bit of jazz —

“Three More Foxes,” “The Fox Hunt,” this and that. So I went with that band for a year. And man, when I got out of that band, I mean it was totally different than DeFranco’s band. This was a bunch of pirates. I mean these guys were half from England, and they didn’t care. I mean the bus used to just throb when it would go down, like we actually rolled a joint I think the length of the bus one time. It went from the front to the back. I mean each guy in the aisle is doing it like this and that. But when I got out of that band man, it was an experience man. Because Maynard was so loose and crazy as hell you know. I mean he had lived with Timothy Leary and experimented with hallucinogenic drugs. And I’d been on the band about a month or so and we would play this place in Cleveland. I can’t remember the name of the high school. But the band director, one of the guys, I’m not mentioning any names, but one of the trumpet players had hit on a high school girl. And we were doing a seminar in the afternoon. A clinic. They called them clinics with Maynard, seminars with Woody. And this band director comes up to Maynard and he said, “look one of your trumpet players was flirting and hitting on one of our high school students and I’ve locked him out of the auditorium, but that’s okay, I’ve got a kid who can cut it.” Well that didn’t sit too well. Maynard went off on this poor guy. He just completely went off on him at the seminar. And then he said, “now we can shake hands and let our trumpet player back in.” It was a job, I felt sorry for the kid, the high school kid who thought he was going to have to play the lead trumpet part and he couldn’t have done it. I mean he could play the high notes but he couldn’t have done that. So we play the concert that night and everything went okay. The band director seemed like an awfully nice guy. Very nice guy. In fact he came up and complimented me highly. I felt sorry for the guy. But we had to leave our band equipment in his band room for

some reason. I don’t remember exactly why. But then in the morning we came to pick it up. Well the English guys, one was — a couple of managers and sound guys and this and that, we brought the bus by to pick up the equipment and somebody said where’s so-and- so face (an expletive face) and the poor girl that was one of his students pointed into the band director’s room. We got our stuff. But these guys had gone through — these English roadies and managers had gone through that high school and placed smoke bombs and different things. Time-set smoke bombs. And we left there and apparently about an hour later they all went off. By the time we got to the next place Willard Alexander’s office, the phone was off the hook. You know Maynard laughed about it. He didn’t care. But I mean they blew the — I said what a band I’m on here, man. This is not Buddy DeFranco and the Glenn Miller Orchestra. Because I mean the Glenn Miller Orchestra had it in the contract if anybody on that band get busted for pot the band folds that night.
